doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Growing up in Verona and Dry Jack
title: Writing the Dry Jack music mostly by ear
summary: Lamb composed by ear and later notated the pieces; Rod Fleeman recently remarked he never wrote anything down.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you laboriously write this music you were writing down with pen and paper?

I wondered about that because we’ll talk about your, the Dry Jack LPs in a moment, but when I heard those tunes and I envisioned writing all those melodies which were pretty complex, and then the other guys learning them.

Yeah it was mostly by ear. I mean I did write the stuff down you know, and made a, it was an effort for me because I learned to play by ear and you know, going back to really crack the code of exactly what I’m writing, you know, in sixteenth notes and — I really had to study that. But not that we used the charts, but I wanted to have it documented somehow and I still have those charts, it’s really funny to look at, you know, the scrawl. But yeah, we just — Rod Fleeman, the guitar player from Dry Jack, I just talked to him three or four days ago and he’s going, “Man you never wrote any of that stuff down.” You know? He brought that up which I had forgotten that it really was about that, about the showing him.
